scenes.headline: Window Specification
scenes.subtitle: Computing across related rows without collapsing them.
scenes.narration: A window specification defines a set of related rows so you can compute across them while keeping every row.

scenes.headline: Window pieces
items: orderBy sets the order within each window
A frame defines which rows are in scope
Rows are kept, unlike a group-by that collapses them
scenes.narration: A window is built from partitionBy to group rows, orderBy to sequence them, and an optional frame to define scope. Crucially, every row is preserved, unlike a group-by that collapses rows into summaries.

scenes.headline: Defining a window spec
scenes.code:
from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

w = Window.partitionBy("dept").orderBy(F.desc("salary"))
df.withColumn("dept_avg", F.avg("salary").over(w)).show()
scenes.narration: We define a window partitioned by department and ordered by salary. Applying avg over that window adds a department average to every row, so each employee sees their team's average while their individual row stays intact.

scenes.headline: Window vs group-by
scenes.narration: Instead of collapsing rows like group-by, a window computes over each row's frame and keeps every original row alongside the new value.

scenes.text: Windows keep every row — that is what sets them apart from group-by.
scenes.narration: The defining trait of a window is that it keeps every row while adding computed values, which distinguishes it from group-by.
